subject: spring-boot
summary: Spring Bootの設定ファイル、Profile別環境分離、@Valueと@ConfigurationPropertiesの比較、設定の優先順位を解説する。
key_points: Profile固有ファイル（application-{profile}.yml）がベースのapplication.ymlを上書きし、環境分離を実現する。
型安全でグループ化された設定バインディングには、@Valueより@ConfigurationPropertiesが推奨される。
設定の優先順位：コマンドライン引数 > 環境変数 > Profile YAML > ベースYAML。
misconceptions: application.yml is completely ignored when a profile-specific file exists.
File-based configuration takes precedence over environment variables.
Mixing YAML and Properties formats in the same project causes no issues.
check_questions: What is the relationship between application.yml and application-prod.yml?
When should you use @ConfigurationProperties instead of @Value?
How should production secrets like database passwords be managed?

fact_candidates: Spring Boot configuration precedence order (CLI > env > profile file > base file)
practical_judgment_candidates: Choosing @Value vs @ConfigurationProperties based on number of related settings
Deciding how to manage secrets in production (env vars / Secret Manager vs hardcoded)
error_interpretation_candidates: Application fails to start because @Value references a missing key with no default
Wrong database connected in production due to missing profile activation
scenario_candidates: Determining which datasource URL is active given CLI args and multiple YAML files
Predicting Java object field values from a given YAML structure with @ConfigurationProperties
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing base application.yml is always overridden entirely by profile files
Thinking environment variables have lower priority than YAML files
